extracted.intended_audience: high-school students, coaches, and organizers interested in the Tournament of Towns math competition
extracted.subtask_description: A brief descriptive summary of the Tournament of Towns high-school math competition: its schedule, levels, problem types, timing, scoring, and answer-checking procedure. Useful for competitors, coaches, and local organizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition levels (O-Level and A-Level)
rubrics_metrics.description: The competition ... is divided into two levels: O-Level (easier) and A-Level (harder).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes difficulty tracks for participants; problems and expectations differ by level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule (Fall and Spring)
rubrics_metrics.description: The competition takes place in the Fall and Spring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two regular sessions per year; participants should prepare for both seasonal rounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format: city-hosted, international
rubrics_metrics.description: The competition is international, but each city hosts its own competition, so participants do not have to travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local organization runs the contest for its city's participants while following the international Tournament of Towns structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem types: proof-based problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of the problems are proof problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect problems requiring written proofs and justificatory reasoning rather than only short numerical answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The time to take the test is 5 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-format contest session; time management and sustained focus are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring: variable points per problem
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of points per problem varies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different problems carry different weights; strategy may involve prioritizing higher-point problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer checking and adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: Afterwards, the answers are checked by the local jury in the city of the competition and/or the Central Jury in Moscow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solutions are subject to local and possibly central review, implying formal judging standards and potential re-checks or appeals.
